explanation: Template specialization in C++ allows developers to define custom implementations of a template for specific types or conditions. It is used to optimize or modify behavior when the general template does not suffice, enabling more precise control over template instantiation and behavior for particular types. This feature is essential for writing flexible, type-safe, and efficient generic code in modern C++.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates template specialization by defining a primary template 'is_error_condition_enum' that defaults to false. It then provides a specialized version for the 'errc' enum type, setting the value to true. When run, it shows how the specialization is used to identify 'errc' as an error condition enum, illustrating how specialization customizes template behavior for specific types in modern C++.
